# Rolling Hash

#### Course: DSA with C++

## Rolling Hash

Let's begin by calculating the hash value of the substring "ABC".

![Calculating the Hash Value for Substring ABC](data:image/png;base64,)

```cpp
Hash(ABC) = Hash(A) + Hash(B) + Hash(C) = 65 + 66 + 67 = 198
```

Next, we will shift the substring one character to the right. This results in another substring, "BCD".

![Calculating the Hash Value for substring BCD](data:image/png;base64,)

In rolling hash, when calculating the hash of a new substring we need to:

- Remove the effect of the old character.
- Add the effect of the new character.

So, now to calculate the hash value of BCD, we'll use the hash value of ABC which we just calculated. Here's how:

```cpp
Hash(BCD) = (Hash(ABC) - Hash(A))  + Hash(D) = (198 - 65)  + 68 = 133 + 68 = 201
```

Since, ABC already contains the substring BC used in ABC, we have removed the effect of A in ABC and added the effect of D which was missing.

In this way, we can calculate the hash values of all substrings of length three.

![Idea Emoji](data:image/png;base64,)

The rolling hash technique makes the string matching process much faster and more efficient.
